title: Desktop Pet Dos系統のウィンドウの一部は、Always On Topの機能を使用できない件。
summary: Always On Top reportedly cannot pin some Desktop Pet DOS-style windows with nonstandard or changing window outlines, but the report does not identify an exact PowerToys version, target application/build, or reproducible window state.

judgment.rationale: The automated upstream triage has already asked the reporter for an English translation, and the current report lacks the exact application identity and reproduction details needed to distinguish an unsupported window type from a PowerToys defect.
evidence: The report identifies Always On Top and Windows Store installation but gives the PowerToys version only as an unknown recent version.
The affected windows are described generally as Desktop Pet DOS-type windows with unusual or changing outlines.
No diagnostic ZIP, exact target application version, or numbered reproduction sequence is provided.
The upstream automation requested an English translation and applied Needs-Author-Feedback.
judgment.recommended_action: Wait for the reporter to answer the existing upstream translation request; then re-triage the exact target window and reproduction.

confidence.rationale: There is not enough application-specific or diagnostic evidence to identify a PowerToys code path or determine whether the target window supports normal topmost semantics.

fix_assessment.rationale: A code fix cannot be scoped until the reporter supplies the requested translation and identifies a reproducible affected application/window.

issue_context.summary: The reporter says Always On Top does not work for some Desktop Pet DOS-style windows whose outline may be nonstandard or variable.
known_information: The affected PowerToy is Always On Top.
PowerToys was installed through Microsoft Store.
The reporter tried multiple methods to apply Always On Top.
The issue is labeled Needs-Author-Feedback and the existing upstream request asks for an English translation.
inferences: The target application may use a nonstandard top-level, layered, child, or transient window, but the current report does not establish which mechanism applies.
The failure may depend on a specific target application build or window state.
issue_context.analysis: Without an exact target application/version and reproducible sequence, maintainers cannot determine which HWND receives the shortcut, whether PowerToys rejects the window, or whether the target immediately clears the topmost state. The existing upstream translation request should be answered before adding another overlapping information request.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body, labels, and upstream automated triage comment.
Confirmed that the report has no diagnostic ZIP, exact PowerToys version, target application version, or detailed reproduction sequence.
Confirmed that upstream already requested an English translation and marked the issue Needs-Author-Feedback.

information_gaps.information: English translation of the report and confirmation of the exact affected application/window.
information_gaps.why_needed: This identifies the product and window behavior that Always On Top must be tested against.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply to the existing upstream request with an English translation and the exact application name/version.

information_gaps.information: Numbered steps showing how the target window is opened and how Always On Top is invoked.
information_gaps.why_needed: This distinguishes shortcut, eligibility, and target-window failures.
